📝 Walkthrough ## Walkthrough This PR enhances the insights operator to dynamically obtain TLS configuration from the OpenShift API server. The workload gatherer and insights client are updated to accept and utilize a config client that fetches TLS security profiles from the API server's configuration. RBAC permissions are expanded to allow reading the `apiservers` resource. ## Changes |Cohort / File(s)|Summary| |---|---| |**RBAC Permission Update**
`manifests/03-clusterrole.yaml`|Added `apiservers` resource to the `config.openshift.io` API group rules for the `insights-operator` ClusterRole, enabling read/write access to API server configuration.| |**Workload Gatherer Integration**
`pkg/gatherers/workloads/gather_workloads_info.go`, `pkg/gatherers/workloads/gather_workloads_runtime_infos.go`, `pkg/gatherers/workloads/gather_workloads_runtime_infos_test.go`|Updated gatherer functions to accept and pass through a config client (`configv1client.Interface`). Modified HTTP client TLS setup to use `GetTLSConfigFromAPIServer(configClient)` instead of inline TLS config construction. Test updated to construct and provide a fake config clientset.| |**TLS Configuration from API Server**
`pkg/insights/insightsclient/apiserver_config.go`, `pkg/insights/insightsclient/apiserver_config_test.go`|New module providing `GetTLSConfigFromAPIServer()` that fetches the `APIServers` cluster resource and derives TLS configuration from the `TLSSecurityProfile`. Includes helper functions to parse TLS versions, resolve TLS profile specs (intermediate/modern/custom), construct cipher suites, and apply security settings. Comprehensive table-driven tests validate TLS version parsing, profile type handling, and cipher suite generation.| |**Insights Client Transport Updates**
`pkg/insights/insightsclient/insightsclient.go`, `pkg/insights/insightsclient/requests.go`, `pkg/insights/insightsclient/requests_test.go`, `pkg/insights/insightsclient/insightsclient_test.go`|Modified `clientTransport()` to accept config client and apply API server–derived TLS config to transport. Updated all request methods (`SendAndGetID`, `RecvReport`, `RecvSCACerts`, `RecvClusterTransfer`, `GetWithPathParam`) to pass config client when setting transport. Reordered imports and normalized whitespace in test files.| ## Estimated code review effort 🎯 4 (Complex) | ⏱️ ~40 minutes
✨ Finishing Touches
🧪 Generate unit tests (beta) - [ ] Create PR with unit tests

> ⚠️ Outside diff range comments (3)
> >
> pkg/insights/insightsclient/insightsclient.go (1)
> > `126-153`: _⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🔴 Critical_ > > **Initialize a fallback `tls.Config` before overlaying APIServer settings.** > > Line 138 can fail and leave `tlsConfig == nil`; with a trusted CA bundle present, Line 150 then dereferences it and panics. This also needs to guard a nil `kubeClient`, so callers can fall back cleanly when the config client is unavailable. > >
> Suggested fix > > ```diff > func clientTransport(authorizer Authorizer, kubeClient configv1client.Interface) http.RoundTripper { > clientTransport := &http.Transport{ > Proxy: authorizer.NewSystemOrConfiguredProxy(), > DialContext: (&net.Dialer{ > Timeout: 30 * time.Second, > KeepAlive: 30 * time.Second, > }).DialContext, > TLSHandshakeTimeout: 10 * time.Second, > DisableKeepAlives: true, > } > > - // Fetch TLS config from API Server > - tlsConfig, err := GetTLSConfigFromAPIServer(kubeClient) > - if err != nil { > - klog.Errorf("getTLSConfigFromAPIServer: %v", err) > - } > + var tlsConfig *tls.Config > + if kubeClient != nil { > + tlsConfig, err = GetTLSConfigFromAPIServer(kubeClient) > + if err != nil { > + klog.Errorf("getTLSConfigFromAPIServer: %v", err) > + } > + } > + if tlsConfig == nil { > + tlsConfig = &tls.Config{} > + } > > // get the cluster proxy trusted CA bundle in case the proxy need it > rootCAs, err := getTrustedCABundle() > if err != nil { > klog.Errorf("Failed to get proxy trusted CA: %v", err) > } > > if rootCAs != nil { > tlsConfig.RootCAs = rootCAs > } > > clientTransport.TLSClientConfig = tlsConfig > ``` >
> > This also needs `crypto/tls` restored in the imports. > >
> 🤖 Prompt for AI Agents > > ``` > Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed. > > In `@pkg/insights/insightsclient/insightsclient.go` around lines 126 - 153, In > clientTransport, ensure tlsConfig is non-nil before using it: if > GetTLSConfigFromAPIServer(kubeClient) returns an error or kubeClient is nil, > initialize tlsConfig = &tls.Config{} as a fallback, then overlay RootCAs from > getTrustedCABundle() only after that check; also restore the crypto/tls import > so tls.Config is available and avoid dereferencing a nil pointer in > clientTransport. > ``` > >
> >

> manifests/03-clusterrole.yaml (1)
> > `73-86`: _⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_ > > **Scope `apiservers` down to read-only access.** > > Line 79 adds `apiservers` to a rule that also grants `create`, `update`, and `patch`, but the new code path only does `APIServers().Get("cluster")`. That gives the operator unnecessary write access to a cluster-critical resource; please split this into a dedicated rule with `resourceNames: ["cluster"]` and `verbs: ["get"]`. > >
> Suggested RBAC change > > ```diff > - apiGroups: > - "config.openshift.io" > resources: > - clusteroperators > - clusteroperators/status > - insightsdatagathers > - - apiservers > verbs: > - create > - get > - update > - patch > - list > - watch > + - apiGroups: > + - "config.openshift.io" > + resources: > + - apiservers > + resourceNames: > + - cluster > + verbs: > + - get > ``` >
> >
> 🤖 Prompt for AI Agents > > ``` > Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed. > > In `@manifests/03-clusterrole.yaml` around lines 73 - 86, The apiservers resource > is currently granted create/update/patch in the same rule; split it into a > dedicated rule that limits access to read-only for the specific object the > operator reads: add a new rule for resource "apiservers" with resourceNames: > ["cluster"] and verbs: ["get"], and remove "apiservers" from the existing rule > that grants create/update/patch so only the remaining resources keep write > access; update the ClusterRole manifest's rules block accordingly (look for the > rule containing apiGroups: ["config.openshift.io"] and the resources list that > includes "apiservers"). > ``` > >
> >
>
> pkg/gatherers/workloads/gather_workloads_runtime_infos.go (1)
> > `60-78`: _⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_ > > **Create the shared HTTP client before fan-out.** > > Line 68 now does a live APIServer lookup via `createHTTPClient`. Doing that inside the per-node goroutine turns a cluster-wide constant into N concurrent control-plane reads, and this branch only logs/returns on failure, so the caller can get partial data with no returned error. Build the client and read the token once before starting workers; `http.Client` is safe to reuse across goroutines. > >
> Possible fix > > ```diff > + httpCli, err := createHTTPClient(configClient) > + if err != nil { > + return nil, []error{fmt.Errorf("failed to initialize the HTTP client: %w", err)} > + } > + tokenData, err := readToken() > + if err != nil { > + return nil, []error{fmt.Errorf("failed to read the serviceaccount token: %w", err)} > + } > + > var wg sync.WaitGroup > wg.Add(len(runtimePodIPs)) > for i := range runtimePodIPs { > go func(podInfo podWithNodeName) { > defer wg.Done() > klog.Infof("Gathering workload runtime info for node %s...\n", podInfo.nodeName) > hostPort := net.JoinHostPort(podInfo.podIP, "8443") > extractorURL := fmt.Sprintf("https://%s/gather_runtime_info", hostPort) > - httpCli, err := createHTTPClient(configClient) > - if err != nil { > - klog.Errorf("Failed to initialize the HTTP client: %v", err) > - return > - } > - tokenData, err := readToken() > - if err != nil { > - klog.Errorf("Failed to read the serviceaccount token: %v", err) > - return > - } > nodeWorkloadCh <- getNodeWorkloadRuntimeInfos(ctx, extractorURL, string(tokenData), httpCli) > }(runtimePodIPs[i]) > } > ``` >
> >
> 🤖 Prompt for AI Agents > > ``` > Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed. > > In `@pkg/gatherers/workloads/gather_workloads_runtime_infos.go` around lines 60 - > 78, The code currently calls createHTTPClient and readToken inside each > goroutine (in the loop over runtimePodIPs), causing N control-plane lookups and > potential partial results; instead, call createHTTPClient(configClient) and > readToken() once before spawning the workers (before wg.Add/loop), fail fast if > either returns an error (log and return the error to the caller), then reuse the > returned http.Client and token string inside each goroutine when calling > getNodeWorkloadRuntimeInfos(ctx, extractorURL, token, httpCli); keep the rest of > the worker logic (nodeWorkloadCh, podWithNodeName, wg) unchanged. > ``` > >
> >
> >
🤖 Prompt for all review comments with AI agents ``` Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed. Inline comments: In `@pkg/gatherers/workloads/gather_workloads_info.go`: - Around line 82-85: The config client construction (configv1client.NewForConfig using g.gatherKubeConfig producing configClient, err) is currently fatal; change it to treat failure as a non-fatal partial error: do not return immediately on error, instead append err to a local errs slice and set configClient to nil (or leave it unset) so the rest of GatherWorkloadsInfo continues to produce the `config/workload_info` record and any runtime info; ensure subsequent code that uses configClient (e.g., calls that fetch TLS profiles or other config APIs) checks for nil and skips those calls when the client is unavailable, and at the end return the assembled records along with the errs slice containing the config client construction error. In `@pkg/insights/insightsclient/apiserver_config.go`: - Around line 16-18: GetTLSConfigFromAPIServer currently uses context.Background() which prevents cancellation; change its signature to accept a caller context (e.g. func GetTLSConfigFromAPIServer(ctx context.Context, configClient configclientset.Interface) (*tls.Config, error)) and use that ctx in the APIServer GET call (configClient.ConfigV1().APIServers().Get(ctx, "cluster", metav1.GetOptions{})); update all call sites to pass their context (or create a short timeout context at the call site if desired) so TLS construction respects deadlines/cancellation. --- Outside diff comments: In `@manifests/03-clusterrole.yaml`: - Around line 73-86: The apiservers resource is currently granted create/update/patch in the same rule; split it into a dedicated rule that limits access to read-only for the specific object the operator reads: add a new rule for resource "apiservers" with resourceNames: ["cluster"] and verbs: ["get"], and remove "apiservers" from the existing rule that grants create/update/patch so only the remaining resources keep write access; update the ClusterRole manifest's rules block accordingly (look for the rule containing apiGroups: ["config.openshift.io"] and the resources list that includes "apiservers"). In `@pkg/gatherers/workloads/gather_workloads_runtime_infos.go`: - Around line 60-78: The code currently calls createHTTPClient and readToken inside each goroutine (in the loop over runtimePodIPs), causing N control-plane lookups and potential partial results; instead, call createHTTPClient(configClient) and readToken() once before spawning the workers (before wg.Add/loop), fail fast if either returns an error (log and return the error to the caller), then reuse the returned http.Client and token string inside each goroutine when calling getNodeWorkloadRuntimeInfos(ctx, extractorURL, token, httpCli); keep the rest of the worker logic (nodeWorkloadCh, podWithNodeName, wg) unchanged. In `@pkg/insights/insightsclient/insightsclient.go`: - Around line 126-153: In clientTransport, ensure tlsConfig is non-nil before using it: if GetTLSConfigFromAPIServer(kubeClient) returns an error or kubeClient is nil, initialize tlsConfig = &tls.Config{} as a fallback, then overlay RootCAs from getTrustedCABundle() only after that check; also restore the crypto/tls import so tls.Config is available and avoid dereferencing a nil pointer in clientTransport. ```
